sections.text: Why this brand gets talked about so much

sections.content: The Ordinary became famous by doing the opposite of everyone else. No glass bottles. No celebrity. The product name is the ingredient and the percentage — niacinamide 10%, glycolic 7%, retinol 0.5% — printed on a plain white label.

For a buyer that is genuinely useful. You can compare two products without guessing what's inside, and you can look up the active before you spend money on it. The packaging looks like a pharmacy and that is the point.
It is also why the brand is so widely copied. A plain white label with simple text is far easier to reproduce than a complex printed box with holograms.

sections.text: The problem with buying it in Pakistan

sections.content: Genuine imported The Ordinary stock in Pakistan costs considerably more than Rs. 1,288. That gap is not a discount somebody found — it is a different supply chain, and the honest thing is to say so plainly.
We cannot verify the origin of branded skincare for you and we are not going to claim we can. What we can do is give you a way to check before money changes hands:

items: Batch code and expiry should be printed on the bottle, not stickered on top
Label text should be sharp. Plain packaging is easy to fake, so print quality is the tell
The dropper on a serum should be glass or good rigid plastic, not soft silicone
Consistency should be thin and watery for a serum. A thick gel is a warning
Buy from someone who takes returns. Ours is 7 days, and cash on delivery lets you look first

sections.content: If you want the imported original with a distributor guarantee, buy it from an authorised retailer and pay what it costs. That is a fair decision. We'd rather you made it knowingly than found out later.

sections.text: Don't buy The Ordinary from us if…

sections.content: You're buying it specifically because you read about one exact active at one exact percentage. If a specific formulation is the whole reason for the purchase, buy the one you researched from a source that guarantees it. A set at this price is a set, and the actives inside may not be the ones in the review you read.
You have sensitive skin and you're planning to introduce several products from the set in the same week. Do one at a time, a week apart, or you'll never know which one caused the reaction.
You expect luxury. There is no bottle weight, no scent, no packaging to photograph. If that's part of what you're paying for, this brand has never offered it.

sections.content: The Ordinary is a good brand that made a simple bargain with its customers: plain packaging, honest labels, lower prices. The trouble with a simple bargain is that it is easy to copy. Buy it from someone who lets you open the parcel before you pay, and check the print on the label — boring advice, but it's the whole game.
